sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from his China Open semi-final against Novak Djokovic after hitting a spectator in the face with a ball. Trailing in the second set, Medvedev swiped at a ball in annoyance after it ricocheted off the back of the court. The ball hit a front-row spectator, who was helped out of the arena. Following discussions with the umpire and an ATP official, Medvedev was disqualified.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Defaults in tennis are rare and occur for code of conduct violations. Although players typically receive multiple warnings before disqualification, Medvedev's offence was severe enough for an instant default. Consequently, he loses his ranking points and prize money from Beijing. The incident highlights ongoing concerns regarding his on-court temper and emotional control.

articles.title: Nigeria mourns 25 killed as military plane crashes into swamp
articles.standfirst: President Bola Tinubu describes the crash as a "painful moment" for the military and the entire nation.

gist: A Nigerian military aircraft crashed into a swamp, killing 32 people on board.
President Bola Tinubu declared three days of national mourning following the crash.
The president has ordered a full investigation into the cause of the crash.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: A military ATR-42 aircraft crashed into a swamp near a naval base in Ondo State on Monday morning. The plane, carrying 25 passengers and seven crew members, was flying from Benin City to Lagos when it went down. All 32 people on board, mostly military personnel, were killed.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: President Bola Tinubu declared three days of national mourning and ordered flags to fly at half-mast. He described the crash as a painful moment for the nation and its armed forces.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: President Tinubu has ordered a full investigation into the crash. Search and rescue efforts at the site are ongoing.
